title: Fibonacci Using Recursion
statement:
The Fibonacci sequence is defined by `F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1` and `F(k) = F(k - 1) + F(k - 2)` for every `k ≥ 2`, so it begins `0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...`.

Given `n`, compute `F(n)`. Because the values grow very quickly, print the result **modulo** `1000000007` (`10^9 + 7`).

The definition is naturally recursive, and interviewers usually ask for it three ways: plain recursion, recursion with memoization, and an iterative loop. Plain recursion makes an exponential number of calls, so it is only fast enough for small `n`; the limits here are chosen so that you have to do better.

**Follow-up:** explain the time and space cost of each of the three versions, and the recursion depth of the memoized one.
hints: Write the plain recursion first and count how many times `F(k)` is recomputed for small `n`; that repetition is the problem.
Either cache each `F(k)` the first time you compute it (memoization), or build the values bottom-up from `F(0)` and `F(1)`.
Going bottom-up you only ever need the previous two values, so two variables are enough. Apply the modulo at every addition.
